It was played on 14 May 2025 between [[AC Milan|Milan]] and [[Bologna FC 1909|Bologna]]. Bologna won the match 1–0 for their third Coppa Italia title, and the first since [[1974 Coppa Italia final|1974]].{{cite web|url=https://www.legaseriea.it/it/media/coppa-italia/il-bologna-conquista-la-coppa-italia-frecciarossa-73mocjo|title=Il Bologna conquista la Coppa Italia Frecciarossa!|publisher=[[Lega Serie A]]|date=14 May 2025|access-date=14 May 2025|language=it}}{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/clyglj8evzgt|title=Bologna edged out AC Milan to win the Coppa Italia, their first major trophy since 1974.|date=15 May 2025|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=15 May 2025}} == Background == [[AC Milan|Milan]] had previously played in fourteen Coppa Italia finals, winning five times. Their most recent final appearance was in [[2018 Coppa Italia final|2018]], a defeat to [[Juventus FC|Juventus]]; their last win was in [[2003 Coppa Italia final|2003]], an aggregate victory over [[AS Roma|Roma]]. Their last single match victory in [[Rome]] dates back to [[1973 Coppa Italia final|1973]] against Juventus. Bologna had won both their two appearances in the cup final; their most recent appearance was a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] victory to [[Palermo FC|Palermo]] in [[1974 Coppa Italia final|1974]]. The two teams had never met in the Coppa Italia final. AC Milan's season turned out to be underwhelming after this Coppa Italia loss, having also finished 8th in the [[2024–25 Serie A|Serie A]]. Bologna finished one spot lower than Milan in the Serie A, but winning this trophy made this season much grander from the perspective of their fans.{{Cite web|url=https://soccerway.com/national/italy/serie-a/20242025/regular-season/r82869/ |title=Serie A |publisher=Soccerway|access-date=26 May 2025}} In reaching the final, both teams qualified for the [[2025–26 Supercoppa Italiana]] (for the first time in Bologna's case). ==Road to the final== ''Note: In all results below, the score of the finalist is given first (H: home; A: away).'' {| width="100%" style="text-align:center" |- valign=top bgcolor=#99ccff !colspan=2 style="width:40%"|[[AC Milan|Milan]] !Round !colspan=2 style="width:40%"|[[Bologna FC 1909|Bologna]] |- valign=top bgcolor=#c1e0ff |Opponent |Result |bgcolor=#c1e0ff|[[2024–25 Coppa Italia]] |Opponent |Result |- |[[US Sassuolo Calcio|Sassuolo]] |6–1 |bgcolor=#c1e0ff|Round of 16 |[[AC Monza|Monza]] |4–0 |- |[[AS Roma|Roma]] |3–1 |bgcolor=#c1e0ff|Quarter-finals |[[Atalanta BC|Atalanta]] |1–0 (A) |- |[[Inter Milan|Internazionale]] |1–1 (H), 3–0 (A)

{{agg|5–1}} |} == Match == === Summary === The game started in front of 68,490 people. In the eighth minute, [[Juan Miranda (footballer)|Juan Miranda]] sent the ball into the penalty area where [[Santiago Castro (footballer, born 2004)|Santiago Castro]] attempted to head the ball beyond [[Mike Maignan]], only for the French goalkeeper to save down his bottom right-hand side and [[Giovanni Fabbian]] unable to convert the rebound.{{Cite web |title=Bologna 1–0 Milan (15 May, 2025) Game Analysis – ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/football/report/_/gameId/724196 |access-date=2025-05-15 |website=ESPN |language=en}}{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=g7oKeH_NtTQ |title=Bologna–Milan 1–0 {{!}} Highlights {{!}} Bologna End 51-year Trophy Wait {{!}} Coppa Italia Frecciarossa 2024/25 |date=2025-05-14 |last=Serie A |access-date=2025-05-15 |via=YouTube}} In the tenth minute, [[Álex Jiménez (footballer, born 2005)|Álex Jiménez]] sent the ball across towards [[Luka Jović]], however Bologna defender [[Sam Beukema]]'s attempted block ended up having to be palmed away by [[Łukasz Skorupski]], before Jović's follow up attempt on the rebound was also stopped by the Polish goalkeeper. In the forty-third minute, a header from [[Emil Holm (footballer)|Emil Holm]] was gathered by Maignan, moments before Milan attempted a quick counter-attack with [[Rafael Leão]] before the Portuguese was caught by a sliding tackle from captain [[Lewis Ferguson]], who received a [[Yellow card (football)|yellow card]] as a result. Neither side made any changes at halftime. In the fifty-third minute, [[Riccardo Orsolini]] was played through on goal before [[Théo Hernandez]] managed to slide the ball away, but only across towards [[Dan Ndoye]] who managed to evade [[Fikayo Tomori]] before striking the ball into the right-hand corner of the net. In the sixty-second minute, Milan made a triple sub, putting on [[Kyle Walker]], [[Santiago Giménez]] and [[João Félix]] for Tomori, Jiménez and Jović. Seven minutes later, Bologna brought on [[Nicolò Casale]] and [[Tommaso Pobega]] for Fabbian and Orsolini. In the seventy-first minute, Hernandez sent a low ball towards Giménez who was waiting in the middle of the penalty area, however the Mexican didn't connect properly with the ball and Skorupski was left to gather what was a tame effort. Bologna made further substitutions, with Holm, Castro and Ndoye all making way for [[Davide Calabria]], [[Jens Odgaard]] and [[Thijs Dallinga]]. Meanwhile Milan, hoping to find a late equaliser, introduced [[Tammy Abraham]] and [[Samuel Chukwueze]] in place of [[Youssouf Fofana (French footballer)|Youssouf Fofana]] and [[Christian Pulisic]]. In the fourth minute of [[injury time]], Odgaard managed to wriggle away from multiple Milan players before striking an effort from outside the penalty area straight into the hands of Maignan. After six minutes of injury time, the game was finished as Bologna won their third Coppa Italia, and their first major trophy since last winning the competition in [[1973–74 Coppa Italia|1974]]. ===
